_generated: Hand-maintained. The local spots pinned on the county map, each tied to one of Christine's OWN videos.
_why: 2026-08-15 (Christine: 'make the map way more detailed for how people would find me - based on
local spots?', then 'how can we make sure we didnt miss any posts? do we have gnome hill in red
feather lakes and the mexican restaurant in berthoud and the lil cafe and inn in drake? - there
are so many').
The map already had a POI layer. It had two pins on it, both golf courses, and both playing the
CITY OF LOVELAND's videos. That is backwards: the reason a buyer should use this map instead of
Zillow's is that the person who drew it has actually eaten, hiked and ridden in these places.
HOW THESE WERE FOUND, because 'did we miss any' is the real question. vidIQ returns roughly the
top 50 popular + 50 recent videos, not all 223 on her channel, so eyeballing those lists was never
going to be complete. What works instead is searching the channel by keyword and reading the
DESCRIPTIONS -- her titles are coy ('Is This the Best Steakhouse in Loveland?') but the
descriptions name the place outright ('Dinner at The Loveland Chophouse'). That one trick placed
the steakhouse, Gnome Road, Route 85 Grill and The Olde Course, all of which the title-only pass
had to skip. Any future addition should be found the same way, not by guessing from a title.
STILL OPEN, and needing her:
- The Mexican restaurant in Berthoud: no video for it surfaced in any channel search. Name it
and it goes straight on.
- The cafe/inn in Drake: this is The River Forks Inn (1601 W Hwy 34), Drake's historic 1905
stage stop -- but it is CLOSED pending new ownership, so it is deliberately NOT pinned. A
recommendation that sends a buyer to a locked door is worse than no pin.
- 'Riding the Harley... to Full Throttle' (J5d3G3PJKxk, 1,463) -- venue unconfirmed.
- Gray's Cafe and BBC Winery in Ault, both named in a listing description but with no dedicated
spot video to attach.
- Her Google Business posts get real views too, but those URLs are not reachable from this
build environment. googlePostUrl exists on every entry, empty, ready to paste rather than
guessed at.
Addresses are what the runtime geocoder resolves (netlify/functions/local-spots.js). Where a
street number could not be verified the business NAME is used as the query instead of a number
typed from memory -- Google resolves those precisely, and a wrong number would pin her personal
recommendation onto someone else's building.
2026-08-15, her own list back: 'sweetheart winder, taste of loveland, colliers hill in erie,
mr chens, erie colorado' -- plus 'yes - loveland chophouse'. That named Horsetooth Reservoir and
the Denver park, which closed two of the open questions above. Still unresolved and needing one
(an annual event whose venue moves, so it is covered by the Downtown Loveland pin rather than
given a fixed one), and the Big Thompson River (a line on the map, not a pin -- see RIVERS).
2026-08-15: the Berthoud restaurant is COCINA & CANTINA, confirmed from her own Google Maps
notification -- 10,000 review views, five stars, posted 7/15/25. Her review text is carried
here verbatim rather than only linked, because Google gives no permalink to a single review: a
link can only open the business's listing and leave a visitor hunting for her among everyone
else's. googleReviewUrl is therefore the PLACE, and the button says 'See It On Google'.
This one entry outweighs every video here: 10,000 views against 14,671 across eighteen videos.
Any future sweep of her local content must include Google reviews, not just YouTube.
Checked and deliberately NOT pinned because both are permanently closed: Grubby'z (Pierce and
Severance), found via a 'replied to your review' email, and The River Forks Inn in Drake.
2026-08-15: she confirmed Bobcat Ridge and Taste of Loveland ('i did bobcat ridge and a taste of
loveland event!'). Bobcat Ridge has no video or review text here yet -- it is pinned on her word
that she contributed there, linking to the place, and the quote + view count can be filled in once
she has the numbers. Taste of Loveland uses the dedicated 'Taste of Loveland 2026' film rather than
the higher-viewed 'All in a day' clip, which is really about three places at once.
2026-08-16: the 'cherry place in west Loveland' is THE COLORADO CHERRY COMPANY -- found the same
way as the others, by reading the video's own description rather than guessing from its title.
That method has now named every spot on this map whose title was coy. Beaver Meadows Resort added
from the same Shorts sweep.
2026-08-16: Sage confirmed by Christine as the bar in the Downtown Loveland video. And her Erie
descriptions named the three she was trying to remember without her having to: '24 Carrot Bistro
and Birdhouse' plus 'teeing off at Colorado National Golf Club'. BIRDHOUSE is the 'one more spot i
cant rememner'. Four spots, none of them guessed -- all read off her own copy.
A video may back more than one spot (the Erie film covers all three). That is honest: the footage
genuinely features each place, and each pin has its own address so they sit correctly on the map.
STILL UNRESOLVED: 'driven' -- no video or description on the channel mentions it.
2026-08-16, systematic mining sweep ('yes mine it!'). Searched the channel by town and by
food/drink terms and read every description. Findings worth recording:
- Eaton Recreation Center added, named in the Eaton video's own description.
- WINDSOR IS GENUINELY EMPTY, not missed. Every Windsor video on the channel is a listing tour
(945 Maplebrook and similar), not a local spot. Its town page has no pins because the footage
does not exist yet -- which is a filming decision, not a data gap.
- A broad food/drink keyword sweep returned nothing new, which suggests the spot videos are
already largely captured. The remaining volume is in her GOOGLE REVIEWS, not YouTube.
2026-08-16 ('do what you can without me'). Her Takeout export landed in Drive but is 206 MB --
far too large to pull through the Drive connector, which returns a file as encoded text. So the
reviews were mined out of GMAIL instead, and Google's own milestone emails turn out to carry the
full review text, the date, the view count AND a real Maps place link. That is everything needed,
with no export required.
Found this way: Dragon Inn in Eaton (4,000+ views -- her second most-read review), A&W in Eaton
(50+, with the root-beer-float-coupon story), plus review text and counts added to Sweet Heart
Winery (1,000+) and Venezia (500+), which already had videos. A spot can carry BOTH a video and a
review; the map credits each platform separately.
Skipped deliberately: her reviews of other REALTORS (Emily Sells Centennial, April Brandon, Jeff
Kurtz, Miranda Cantin, Alissa Rhoades). Real reviews, but colleagues rather than local spots, and
pinning a competing agent on her own map would be an odd thing to do to her.

spots.name: Sweet Heart Winery
spots.blurb: A big red barn on the Big Thompson, 2.5 miles west of town at the mouth of the canyon. Christine has said outright it's one of the reasons she moved back to Loveland.
spots.videoTitle: Sweetheart Winery is one reason I moved back to Loveland
spots.reviewQuote: Sweetheart Winery in Loveland isn't just a venue; it's a memorable experience woven into the fabric of my personal and professional life. I chose Sweetheart Winery for my client appreciation party and my daughter's bridal shower. Both events were nothing short of magical, thanks to the breathtaking setting, exceptional service, and exquisite wines.

spots.name: El Pueblito Mexican Restaurant
spots.blurb: Christine's most-watched restaurant video — a straight, unsponsored look at a Loveland Mexican spot locals already know.
spots.videoTitle: #elpueblito loveland restaurants

spots.name: Mr. Chen Sushi & Hibachi Steak House
spots.blurb: Tucked at the end of a strip mall on Eisenhower, and better than that makes it sound. Christine's first visit is on camera, verdict included.
spots.videoTitle: Trying Sushi at Mr. Chen for the First Time! Would I eat here again?

spots.name: Devil's Backbone Open Space
spots.address: Devil's Backbone Open Space, Hidden Valley Dr
spots.blurb: The rock fin west of town and the trail most new Loveland residents walk first. Three things worth knowing before you go — from someone who has.
spots.videoTitle: If you're planning to hike Devil's Backbone, here are 3 things you NEED to know

spots.name: Downtown Loveland

spots.name: Venezia Italian Restaurant & Bar
spots.blurb: Family-run, twenty-plus pastas, and a square pizza the regulars come back for — in a farm town of about 5,000 people.
spots.videoTitle: Venezia: Eaton's Best Italian Restaurant

spots.name: Eaton Country Club

spots.videoTitle: Inside the Eaton Country Club with Mccarty's: A Hidden Gem

spots.name: Downtown Ault
spots.blurb: Christine grew up around here and films it that way — the dining and the small-town character behind a name most buyers drive straight past.
spots.videoTitle: Discover Ault: Hidden Gems and Local Dining Spots!

spots.name: Red Feather Lakes
spots.blurb: An hour and a bit up from Fort Collins and a different Colorado entirely. Her longer film on it is one of her best-watched local pieces.
spots.videoTitle: Red Feather Lakes: The Hidden Gem of Colorado

spots.name: Poudre Canyon & the Baldwin Tunnel
spots.blurb: The hand-cut tunnel on Highway 14 above Fort Collins, filmed from the back of a Harley. This is the drive that sells Northern Colorado to people who've only seen photos.
spots.videoTitle: Riding Through the Historic Baldwin Tunnel – Poudre Canyon, Colorado

spots.name: The Loveland Chophouse
spots.blurb: The downtown steakhouse behind her 'best steakhouse in Loveland' video — filmed the night she celebrated a closing there.
spots.videoTitle: Is This the Best Steakhouse in Loveland?

spots.name: Gnome Road (Elf Lane)
spots.blurb: The stretch above Red Feather where tiny gnome houses are tucked into the trees. Locals know it; buyers relocating here have never heard of it.
spots.videoTitle: Where Is Red Feather Lakes? Exploring Colorado's Hidden Gem & Gnome Road!

spots.name: The Olde Course at Loveland
spots.blurb: Northwest Loveland's municipal course and the neighbourhood around it — mature fairways, a renovated clubhouse, and homes that hold their value.
spots.videoTitle: Why Loveland Buyers Love The Olde Course | Colorado Golf Living

spots.name: Route 85 Grill
spots.blurb: Eaton's newer grill on the highway through town, filmed around its opening — part of why a 5,000-person farm town is worth a second look.
spots.videoTitle: Unveiling Eaton, Colorado: Hidden Gem with Gelato, Fun & Family

spots.name: Horsetooth Reservoir

spots.reviewQuote: Berthoud's Gem for Mexican Food! Cocina & Cantina in Berthoud totally surprised me—in the best way. The food is beautifully presented, the ingredients are fresh, and the flavors were spot on.

spots.name: Bobcat Ridge Natural Area
spots.blurb: Fort Collins-owned open space on the west side of Loveland — ponderosa, old homestead ruins and a long loop most new residents never find.

spots.name: Taste of Loveland

spots.videoTitle: What Makes Loveland's Cherry Treats So Special?

spots.name: 24 Carrot Bistro

spots.videoTitle: Why Everyone Loves Living in Erie Colorado!

spots.name: A&W Restaurant
spots.blurb: Where Christine takes out-of-town buyers to talk about Eaton over a root beer float — she hands out free float coupons.
